notes.decision: Per accumulated vocabulary, ⲡⲧⲭⲁⲓ̈ = 'the abode' (tentative) — distinct from ⲡⲭⲁⲓ̈ 'the world.' Used here as a third item of comparison in the chapter title alongside First Man and Ambassador.

Tentatively rendered 'set out after / pursue.' The construction ⲥⲁ 'after' parallels line 32 ⲉⲓ ⲥⲁ 'came after,' suggesting a verb of pursuit. ⲁ⳨ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ may be ⲁⲣⲟⲩⲱ/ⲁⲣⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ 'to occupy oneself with, ply, follow up.'
Tentatively 'to seek them out / to redeem them' — fits the typological context (the father descending after his lost sons). May be Lyc form of ϣⲓⲛⲉ 'seek' or ⲥⲱⲧⲉ 'redeem' with 3pl object suffix.

Translated 'shines forth in the Sweetness.' ⲧⲣⲓ̈ⲉ tentatively read as a verb related to ⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'shine, radiate' (cf. ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance' in glossary). ⲡⲭⲗⲥⲉ per accumulated vocabulary = 'sweetness' (Lyc. for ϩⲗⲟϭ); functions here as cosmological locus = the Land of Sweetness/Light. Could alternatively represent ⲡⲭⲥⲉ 'the Height' with intrusive ⲗ; either reading yields a divine-realm locative.

Rendered 'performing the fourth (watch).' ϩⲧⲟⲉ per accumulated vocab = 'fourth, quarter (of night).' The phrase remains opaque without more context — the Two Sons / Living Soul performing some quartered cosmic office.

Translated 'furnace.' Unattested lexeme; reading from context (sun-ship simile + 'the great Spirit dwells within') requires a glowing/contained vessel. Possibly related to ⲃⲣⲏⲣⲉ 'kiln' (Crum) or a Lycopolitan variant. The image is the sun-ship as a great fiery container with the Spirit blazing within.

Translated 'dwells.' Verbal stem unidentified; possibly = ⲱϣ qualitative (be poured forth, abide) with prosthetic ⲍ-, or related to a verb of containment/blazing. The cosmological context is the great Spirit's indwelling presence within the cosmic vessel.
Per accumulated vocabulary: 'unto the foot of' = supervisory/rescue arrival into someone's presence. Here describes the warrior-man entering the captive prince's place to free him.

Translated 'yet again.' Phrase unattested; possibly a Lycopolitan compound adverb meaning 'at this moment also' or a discourse-marker introducing a follow-up teaching. Functionally parallel to ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ.

Two parallel agentive compounds: 'choosers' (ⲣⲉϥ-ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄) and 'redeemers' (ⲣⲉϥ-ⲥⲱⲧⲉ). The disciples are exhorted to be both selectors and redeemers of their own souls — paralleling the apostle's two functions.

Tentatively rendered 'impassibility.' Best parsed as Greek ἀπάθεια / ἀπαθής 'without passion, impassible' adapted to Coptic with -ⲏⲧ ending. The phrase '[impassibility?] of the eyes of the light' fits a Manichaean spiritual register. Alternative: a native compound on -ϩⲏⲧ 'heart' (e.g. ⲁⲧ-ϩⲏⲧ).
